# Mission kits

Generated by tools/missions.mjs. Scenario settings are design values, not doctrine. Nothing has been played.

- [Hedgerow fields, Normandy 1944](hedgerow.md): Tanks and infantry clear one field at a time, each covering the other.
- [Hold the reverse slope](ridge.md): Defend behind the crest and counterattack troops that come over it.
- [Forest road in winter](motti.md): A road-bound force in forest is ambushed in pieces.
- [Encircle the town, 1944](town-ring.md): Fix the town frontally and send the main blow round it.
- [Noise in front, attack on the flank, 1942](jungle-flank.md): Don't swing the whole defence to face the noise; keep a reserve for the flank.
- [Break a bunker line](bunker-line.md): Fire on the embrasures and smoke the bunker's neighbours while engineers close in.
- [Force a river line](river.md): Cross wide on a screened front and dig in on the far bank before the counterattack.
- [Retake the village at dawn](lost-village.md): Consolidate quickly, and counterattack before the enemy has.
- [Night attack on a perimeter](night-raid.md): Short vision favours whoever is closest and quietest. MGs on fixed lines hold the perimeter.
- [Pursue a withdrawing enemy](breakout.md): Push a fast group past the rearguard. The withdrawal is always ordered, not left to auto-move.
missions.breakout:
# Pursue a withdrawing enemy

**Teaches:** Push a fast group past the rearguard. The withdrawal is always ordered, not left to auto-move.

**Map needs:** open country, crossroads, a delay line. **Win:** The defender gets half its force past the crossroads flag.

## Sides
**Attacker:** What-if: modern ideas on a WW2 force, company shape, fidelity 0. Not period play: re-plans on events, commits the reserve behind success. For comparison against period personas.
**Defender:** German battle group, 1944 (reported doctrine), company shape, fidelity 0.7. Aggressive counterattacks; dangerous to push into. German doctrine here is reported by other nations.
  - Counterattack a lost position at once, close behind the fire, at the flank of the break-in.
  - Build strongpoints round MGs, heavy mortars and an SP gun, firing all round.
  - One narrow main effort with the heavy weapons massed behind it.

## Doctrine
- **Pursuit:** When the enemy breaks, pursue at once without waiting for neighbours. Press on a broad front against his flanks, take the shortest routes to cut his retreat, and push guns and machine guns forward so he cannot re-form. Bypass obstacles and cut off rearguards. Only a senior commander halts it.
- **Delay and withdrawal:** Leave before rifle fire pins you and before the enemy can assault. By day each echelon covers the last in turn. On a delaying position a company holds twice its normal frontage and opens at extreme range, 800 to 1,200 yards, to force deployment, then goes.

## What a good bot does
- **Pursue at once, broad and fast, to a set limit** (tac.pursuit)
  - Go at once with the nearest fast units; don't wait for neighbours.
  - Press on a broad front against his flanks; send groups by the shortest routes to cut his retreat.
  - Bring MGs, mortars and guns forward so he can't re-form.
  - Bypass strongpoints and rearguards; stop at a set limit (his next prepared line or own support range) and consolidate.
- **Leave early, covering in turn** (tac.withdrawal)
  - Go before the enemy is within 0.5 x rifle or rifle fire is hurting you.
  - One part covers while the rest moves, then swap. Last out has a covered route.
  - Delay: spread wide, fire from maximum range, then go when he deploys.
  - Successive lines no farther apart than 1.0 x mg, so each covers the last.
  - The withdrawal is an order in both mods. Auto-move only: vanilla idle soldiers may also fall back alone, so expect leaks; RobZ idle soldiers never do (no_retreat).

Figure: 4-layers/svg/f-pursuit.svg
missions.bunker-line:
# Break a bunker line

**Teaches:** Fire on the embrasures and smoke the bunker's neighbours while engineers close in.

**Map needs:** bunkers, wire, open ground. **Win:** The attacker destroys or takes two of three bunkers.

## Sides
**Attacker:** US rifle battalion, 1944, company shape, fidelity 0.6. Methodical; strong with support weapons, slow without them.
  - Lead with fire: mortars and MGs on the objective before any rifle squad moves.
  - Put the main line on the reverse slope when the forward slope is under observed fire.
  - Counter infiltration with posts that hold alone and a reserve that strikes hard.
**Defender:** German battle group, 1944 (reported doctrine), platoon shape, fidelity 0.7. Aggressive counterattacks; dangerous to push into. German doctrine here is reported by other nations.
  - Counterattack a lost position at once, close behind the fire, at the flank of the break-in.
  - Build strongpoints round MGs, heavy mortars and an SP gun, firing all round.
  - One narrow main effort with the heavy weapons massed behind it.

## Doctrine
- **Pillbox and bunker assault:** Find the pillbox by its embrasures and where it can flank the approach. Guns and machine guns hold its embrasures, smoke blinds it, a wire party cuts a lane, then the assault party closes with flame and charges. Others bypass it and watch its exits. When it falls silent, the attack goes on at once.
- **Smoke:** Smoke goes on the enemy, not in front of yourself. US tests gave a four-to-one fire advantage that way. Wind decides: a steady light breeze is best, and wind blowing toward you rules it out except in withdrawal. Rounds last seconds to minutes, so time smoke to the move. Use HE on located targets and smoke on unlocated ones.

## What a good bot does
- **Hold the embrasures, blind it, cut a lane, close from the flank** (tac.pillbox)
  - Find it: embrasures, and where it can flank the approach.
  - Guns, tanks or MGs fire on the embrasures from a flank; smoke blinds the rest.
  - Engineers clear wire or mines; the assault party closes from the side the embrasures don't cover, with flame or charges.
  - Other units bypass it and watch its exits; once it is silent, the attack continues at once.
- **Smoke on the enemy, timed to the move** (tac.smoke)
  - Located target in range: HE. Unlocated or out of range: smoke on it or its field of view.
  - Smoke the enemy weapon, never a curtain in front of own units.
  - Start just before the move, keep it up until cover: rounds = (gap / speed) / profile smoke life (vanilla about 60 s, RobZ grenade about 90 s).
  - Skip if it blinds own overwatch or a neighbour's lane. Wind moves no smoke in game, so doctrine wind rules drop out.
  - Enemy smoke: laid weapons keep firing on approaches; reserve moves up.
- **Lift late, shift guns to the flanks** (tac.assault-timing)
  - Close to the nearest point that doesn't mask supporting fire, then assault.
  - Before that, move guns toward the flank of the resistance, so they fire longest.
  - When masked, mg and mortars shift to enemy beside or behind the objective.
  - Assault together. A piecemeal assault loses much of its effect.

Figure: 4-layers/svg/f-pillbox.svg
missions.hedgerow:
# Hedgerow fields, Normandy 1944

**Teaches:** Tanks and infantry clear one field at a time, each covering the other.

**Map needs:** small fields, hedges, sunken lanes. **Win:** Attacker takes three field flags in turn before time runs out.

## Sides
**Attacker:** US rifle battalion, 1944, company shape, fidelity 0.6. Methodical; strong with support weapons, slow without them.
  - Lead with fire: mortars and MGs on the objective before any rifle squad moves.
  - Put the main line on the reverse slope when the forward slope is under observed fire.
  - Counter infiltration with posts that hold alone and a reserve that strikes hard.
**Defender:** German battle group, 1944 (reported doctrine), platoon shape, fidelity 0.7. Aggressive counterattacks; dangerous to push into. German doctrine here is reported by other nations.
  - Counterattack a lost position at once, close behind the fire, at the flank of the break-in.
  - Build strongpoints round MGs, heavy mortars and an SP gun, firing all round.
  - One narrow main effort with the heavy weapons massed behind it.

## Doctrine
- **Tank company attack, with infantry:** Envelop as the rule: support elements fire from the front while the company moves under cover to a flank or rear. Attack frontally only when forced. Against a fortified position or tank obstacles the infantry goes first. Leading platoons assault together, about 300 yards or less out, once anti-tank weapons are gone.
- **Company attack:** Don't advance evenly. Push part of the company through the best-covered ground into a weak spot while the rest press and split the enemy's effort. Usually two platoons lead and one is held back. An interior company's zone is 200 to 500 yards, at most what its leaders can control.

## What a good bot does
- **Tanks envelop; infantry first if obstacles** (tac.tank-infantry)
  - Default: support fires frontally, tanks go under cover to a flank.
  - Known AT obstacles or fortifications: infantry first, tanks fire from behind.
  - When tanks lead, infantry follows at once, in small groups clear of the tanks.
  - Assault only once AT weapons are gone; all together.
  - Stalled: fall back to a rally point and retry.
- **Something fires while something moves** (tac.fire-and-move)
  - Split: base of fire pins, maneuver moves. They may swap.
  - Site the base to fire obliquely, about 0.6 to 0.8 x mg from the objective (design).
  - Maneuver goes by a covered route that isn't the obvious one, never a wide loop in the open.
  - Keep on the first post; detach the least possible to answer flank fire.
- **Assault guns at the main effort, tank destroyers kept out of close combat** (tac.assault-gun)
  - Assault guns go with the infantry of the main effort, firing HE on the points that hold it up.
  - Tank destroyers wait in overwatch for tanks, away from close enemy infantry, with their own infantry or MG cover.
  - Either can fire on bunkers once enemy AT is suppressed.

Figure: 4-layers/svg/f-tank-attack.svg
missions.jungle-flank:
# Noise in front, attack on the flank, 1942

**Teaches:** Don't swing the whole defence to face the noise; keep a reserve for the flank.

**Map needs:** jungle or dense woods, one track. **Win:** The attacker takes the rear flag.

## Sides
**Attacker:** Japanese infantry, 1942 (reported doctrine), company shape, fidelity 0.8. Flanking and night attacks; at high fidelity it charges when losing. All doctrine here is reported by the US and UK.
  - Fake strength in front with noise and automatic fire while the main force goes round a flank.
  - Under a holding attack, send LMG and grenade patrols round the flanks into the rear.
  - Prefer attacks when vision is short.
  - When a group is losing, charge instead of falling back. (larp lore)
**Defender:** British infantry battalion, 1944, platoon shape, fidelity 0.6. Careful and smoke-heavy; rarely overextends.
  - Screen every crossing of open ground; move once the smoke is thick.
  - Consolidate at once on each objective before the next bound.

## Doctrine
- **Bait and deception:** Make the enemy show himself with a bait, such as a dummy, decoy, feint, noise or a weapon firing to provoke a reply, then kill what answered with a hidden weapon. Refuse his bait. Only named guns engage decoys and scouts, and the rest hold to the set range. Dummies work only if plausible and well clear of real works.
- **Infiltration and its counter:** Small, heavily armed groups slip through unwatched or "impassable" ground, often in darkness or fog, while the main attack holds the defender. They take the start line or strike from behind. The counter is self-contained posts that fight all round, used as pivots for reserves that hunt the infiltrators.

## What a good bot does
- **Bait to find him, hold fire against his bait** (tac.bait)
  - A cheap element shows itself or fires; hidden killers are laid where a reply would come from and hit it at once.
  - Only units named for it engage scouts and lone vehicles; AT guns hold to the set range.
  - Feint on a second axis; if it finds weakness it becomes the main effort.
  - Withdrawing: a few weapons keep firing to mimic the position.
  - Ambush in close ground or defiles: open close, keep a way out, never chase.
- **Pass small groups through unwatched ground; counter with all-round posts** (tac.infiltration)
  - Attack: send a small, well-armed group (SMG, MG, light mortar) along the unwatched route while the main attack holds the front.
  - Its targets are the enemy's rear: heavy weapons, AT guns, crews, and the line the main attack must cross.
  - Defense: every post can fire all round; do not pull posts back when infiltrators appear.
  - Use the reserve to hunt the infiltrators, pivoting on the posts.
- **Keep a support, spend it whole, rebuild it** (tac.reserve)
  - Exposed flank or unclear enemy: hold back more, up to two of three groups.
  - Hold while fires or other groups can restart the attack.
  - Commit whole, at once, at a flank or at weakness; never reinforce strong resistance.
  - Then rebuild one from relieved or stray units.

Figure: 4-layers/svg/f-infiltration.svg
missions.lost-village:
# Retake the village at dawn

**Teaches:** Consolidate quickly, and counterattack before the enemy has.

**Map needs:** village, orchards. **Win:** The defender has just taken the village. The attacker must retake it, and the defender must consolidate in time.

## Sides
**Attacker:** German battle group, 1944 (reported doctrine), company shape, fidelity 0.7. Aggressive counterattacks; dangerous to push into. German doctrine here is reported by other nations.
  - Counterattack a lost position at once, close behind the fire, at the flank of the break-in.
  - Build strongpoints round MGs, heavy mortars and an SP gun, firing all round.
  - One narrow main effort with the heavy weapons massed behind it.
**Defender:** US rifle battalion, 1944, company shape, fidelity 0.6. Methodical; strong with support weapons, slow without them.
  - Lead with fire: mortars and MGs on the objective before any rifle squad moves.
  - Put the main line on the reverse slope when the forward slope is under observed fire.
  - Counter infiltration with posts that hold alone and a reserve that strikes hard.

## Doctrine
- **Counterattack:** A penetration is fought at once by the support, by fire or by counterattack, and it must land before the enemy organizes. It strikes his flank in maximum force, while fires across the base of the penetration stop more from entering. Pursuit past the old line is by fire only.
- **Company defense:** Stop the enemy by fire ahead of the line, and meet those who arrive in close combat. Two platoons forward and one in support, positions covering each other in width and depth. Frontage runs from 500 yards in close ground to 800 to 1,000 in the open, about double an attack zone.

## What a good bot does
- **Hit the flank before he organizes** (tac.counterattack)
  - Go at once, whole, at the flank of the penetration.
  - Fire across its base to stop more entering.
  - Stop at the old line. Beyond it, fire only.
  - Enemy armor seen near and able to reach it: keep the reserve, hold a flank line, and use tac.at-screen.
- **Go past the objective, then dig in** (tac.consolidate)
  - Don't stop on it: move a short way past (design 0.1 to 0.2 x rifle).
  - Bring mg and light AT up at once to cover front and open flanks.
  - If not advancing, set all-round defense and enter cover.
  - Clear the whole objective.
- **Keep a support, spend it whole, rebuild it** (tac.reserve)
  - Exposed flank or unclear enemy: hold back more, up to two of three groups.
  - Hold while fires or other groups can restart the attack.
  - Commit whole, at once, at a flank or at weakness; never reinforce strong resistance.
  - Then rebuild one from relieved or stray units.

Figure: 4-layers/svg/f-counterattack.svg
missions.motti:
# Forest road in winter

**Teaches:** A road-bound force in forest is ambushed in pieces.

**Map needs:** snow, dense forest, one road. **Win:** The column reaches the far road flag, or the defender cuts it into two or more pieces.

## Sides
**Attacker:** Soviet rifle regiment, summer 1941, company shape, fidelity 0.9. Larp lore, not doctrine: frontal and costly on purpose. Its own manuals asked for initiative; this persona plays the 1941 reputation.
  - Attack straight down the ordered axis; do not shift to a found gap. (larp lore)
  - Hold or counterattack; withdraw only on a direct order from the top. (larp lore)
  - Feed the reserve into a stalled attack rather than holding it back. (larp lore)
**Defender:** Finnish battalion, winter 1939-40, platoon shape, fidelity 0.8. Needs a mod with a Finnish army or a winter map; maps to no stock army. Finnish practice here is reported.
  - Use snipers heavily from hides, as reported of Finnish practice.
  - Ambush road-bound columns from the woods.
  - Cut a stalled column into pockets and destroy them one by one. (larp lore)

## Doctrine
- **Winter fighting:** Thin evidence, Soviet only. Villages and woods matter more in winter, troops move slower off roads, and nights last longer. Deny the enemy shelter. Ski troops bypass and envelop. Without time to dig, build snow parapets; ice and charges go on tank approaches.
- **Ambush:** Lay the ambush in close ground on the enemy’s approach, on both sides of the route but staggered so no one hits his own. Let the scouts pass; the leader opens with rapid fire, best shots on leaders, men told off for vehicles. Strike hard, take prisoners, and leave before he recovers.

## What a good bot does
- **Ambush in close ground, open on the main body, leave fast** (tac.ambush)
  - Two or more parties on both sides of the route, staggered so their fire does not cross into each other.
  - Hold fire until the main body is in close range; let the scouts through.
  - One unit opens the ambush, all fire at once; first targets are leaders, AT crews and vehicles stopped by mines.
  - Against tanks: mine or block the lead and rear vehicles first.
  - Strike, then leave by a planned covered route before the enemy can reply in strength; never chase.
- **In winter, shelter and roads decide** (tac.winter)
  - Value villages and woods more when choosing axes and held points.
  - Expect slow off-road flanks; plan shorter maneuvers.
  - Check tank routes before committing them.
- **Snipers hunt hidden weapons and leaders; watch roofs and tempt fire** (tac.counter-sniper)
  - Own sniper: forward or on a flank, apart from the platoon; first targets are MG crews, AT crews, officers and spotters.
  - Move after firing or after a miss; mark targets for MGs and mortars.
  - Against enemy snipers: watch roofs, towers and steeples; clear them early.
  - Find a hidden enemy with searching fire or a cheap unit moving to tempt a shot, then answer with HE.

Figure: 4-layers/svg/f-ambush.svg
missions.night-raid:
# Night attack on a perimeter

**Teaches:** Short vision favours whoever is closest and quietest. MGs on fixed lines hold the perimeter.

**Map needs:** night or fog, perimeter, scrub. **Win:** The attacker takes the command-post flag.

## Sides
**Attacker:** Japanese infantry, 1942 (reported doctrine), company shape, fidelity 0.8. Flanking and night attacks; at high fidelity it charges when losing. All doctrine here is reported by the US and UK.
  - Fake strength in front with noise and automatic fire while the main force goes round a flank.
  - Under a holding attack, send LMG and grenade patrols round the flanks into the rear.
  - Prefer attacks when vision is short.
  - When a group is losing, charge instead of falling back. (larp lore)
**Defender:** US rifle battalion, 1944, platoon shape, fidelity 0.6. Methodical; strong with support weapons, slow without them.
  - Lead with fire: mortars and MGs on the objective before any rifle squad moves.
  - Put the main line on the reverse slope when the forward slope is under observed fire.
  - Counter infiltration with posts that hold alone and a reserve that strikes hard.

## Doctrine
- **Night attack:** Reconnoiter at least the night before. Go straight at the objective: mixing frontal attack and envelopment at night usually produces confusion and friendly fire. Stay in column until 100 to 200 yards out, silent and marked. Units stopped by darkness dig in all-round.

## What a good bot does
- **Night or low vision means straight ahead and simple** (tac.night)
  - Keep groups in column and deploy only close to the objective.
  - No envelopment: one direct assault on a point already scouted.
  - Narrow each weapon's sector and raise density on the line.
  - A group that stops loses its order: set all-round defense where it stands.
  - Patrol the gaps between held points.
- **Machine guns in enfilade, crossing fire, no gap at the flanks** (tac.mg-defense)
  - Site MGs on the flanks of the position, firing across the front, not straight ahead.
  - Neighbouring MGs' fields cross; check each flank is covered.
  - Heavy MGs take the long fixed lines; light MGs fill the gaps near posts.

Figure: 4-layers/svg/f-night.svg
missions.ridge:
# Hold the reverse slope

**Teaches:** Defend behind the crest and counterattack troops that come over it.

**Map needs:** ridge, open forward slope. **Win:** Defender holds the crest-line flag to the end.

## Sides
**Attacker:** German battle group, 1944 (reported doctrine), company shape, fidelity 0.7. Aggressive counterattacks; dangerous to push into. German doctrine here is reported by other nations.
  - Counterattack a lost position at once, close behind the fire, at the flank of the break-in.
  - Build strongpoints round MGs, heavy mortars and an SP gun, firing all round.
  - One narrow main effort with the heavy weapons massed behind it.
**Defender:** British infantry battalion, 1944, platoon shape, fidelity 0.6. Careful and smoke-heavy; rarely overextends.
  - Screen every crossing of open ground; move once the smoke is thick.
  - Consolidate at once on each objective before the next bound.

## Doctrine
- **Reverse-slope defense:** When the enemy can watch the forward slope, put the main position behind the crest. Outposts hold the forward slope; heavy weapons and most troops wait behind and fire onto the crest as the enemy tops it. Woods give the same cover. The risk: lose the crest and you lose the view.
- **Counterattack:** A penetration is fought at once by the support, by fire or by counterattack, and it must land before the enemy organizes. It strikes his flank in maximum force, while fires across the base of the penetration stop more from entering. Pursuit past the old line is by fire only.

## What a good bot does
- **Hold behind the crest when the forward slope is watched** (tac.reverse-slope)
  - Main position just behind the crest, out of sight of enemy units beyond close range; weapons laid on the crest line.
  - One or two outposts on the forward slope or crest to see and warn; they fall back on contact.
  - Most of the force held back as a counterattack group aimed at the crest.
  - If the crest is lost, counterattack it at once: whoever holds it sees the whole position.
  - Woods count as a reverse slope; sit back from the wood edge, not on it.
- **Hit the flank before he organizes** (tac.counterattack)
  - Go at once, whole, at the flank of the penetration.
  - Fire across its base to stop more entering.
  - Stop at the old line. Beyond it, fire only.
  - Enemy armor seen near and able to reach it: keep the reserve, hold a flank line, and use tac.at-screen.
- **Machine guns in enfilade, crossing fire, no gap at the flanks** (tac.mg-defense)
  - Site MGs on the flanks of the position, firing across the front, not straight ahead.
  - Neighbouring MGs' fields cross; check each flank is covered.
  - Heavy MGs take the long fixed lines; light MGs fill the gaps near posts.

Figure: 4-layers/svg/f-reverse-slope.svg
missions.river:
# Force a river line

**Teaches:** Cross wide on a screened front and dig in on the far bank before the counterattack.

**Map needs:** river, one bridge, fords. **Win:** The attacker holds a far-bank flag for the last third of the match.

## Sides
**Attacker:** Soviet Guards rifle division, 1944, company shape, fidelity 0.7. Heavy, fast main blow and bold exploitation.
  - Mass most forces and fire on the main blow where ground gives cover and observation.
  - On finding a gap, leaders push through on their own, even off direction.
  - Fix a town frontally with part; send the main blow round to its rear.
**Defender:** German battle group, 1944 (reported doctrine), platoon shape, fidelity 0.7. Aggressive counterattacks; dangerous to push into. German doctrine here is reported by other nations.
  - Counterattack a lost position at once, close behind the fire, at the flank of the break-in.
  - Build strongpoints round MGs, heavy mortars and an SP gun, firing all round.
  - One narrow main effort with the heavy weapons massed behind it.

## Doctrine
- **River crossing:** Lead companies cross by boat, reserves by bridge. Form boat groups early and keep tactical unity. Normally three platoons abreast, with weapons following once they land. Hold fire on the water, rally on prominent features, clear the bank fast. Advance guards may simply cross by surprise.

## What a good bot does
- **Crossings are chokes; several points, then rally** (tac.crossing)
  - Cover the far bank with fire before anything crosses.
  - Cross at more than one point when the map allows.
  - Infantry first, abreast; heavy weapons and vehicles after the far bank holds.
  - Rally on the first prominent feature; don't stop on the bank.
  - Lead elements take an undefended crossing at once rather than waiting.
- **Smoke on the enemy, timed to the move** (tac.smoke)
  - Located target in range: HE. Unlocated or out of range: smoke on it or its field of view.
  - Smoke the enemy weapon, never a curtain in front of own units.
  - Start just before the move, keep it up until cover: rounds = (gap / speed) / profile smoke life (vanilla about 60 s, RobZ grenade about 90 s).
  - Skip if it blinds own overwatch or a neighbour's lane. Wind moves no smoke in game, so doctrine wind rules drop out.
  - Enemy smoke: laid weapons keep firing on approaches; reserve moves up.
- **Go past the objective, then dig in** (tac.consolidate)
  - Don't stop on it: move a short way past (design 0.1 to 0.2 x rifle).
  - Bring mg and light AT up at once to cover front and open flanks.
  - If not advancing, set all-round defense and enter cover.
  - Clear the whole objective.

missions.town-ring:
# Encircle the town, 1944

**Teaches:** Fix the town frontally and send the main blow round it.

**Map needs:** town, open approaches, roads behind. **Win:** The attacker takes the road flag behind the town and the town centre.

## Sides
**Attacker:** Soviet Guards rifle division, 1944, battalion shape, fidelity 0.7. Heavy, fast main blow and bold exploitation.
  - Mass most forces and fire on the main blow where ground gives cover and observation.
  - On finding a gap, leaders push through on their own, even off direction.
  - Fix a town frontally with part; send the main blow round to its rear.
**Defender:** German battle group, 1944 (reported doctrine), company shape, fidelity 0.7. Aggressive counterattacks; dangerous to push into. German doctrine here is reported by other nations.
  - Counterattack a lost position at once, close behind the fire, at the flank of the break-in.
  - Build strongpoints round MGs, heavy mortars and an SP gun, firing all round.
  - One narrow main effort with the heavy weapons massed behind it.

## Doctrine
- **Clearing a village:** A fire section suppresses the main street; clearing sections alternate through the houses, entering from the back, top floor downward. Don't encircle: an escape route onto a killing ground beats desperate defenders. Thin evidence, nearly all from one UK manual.
- **Assault guns and tank destroyers:** Assault guns go to the main effort to help the infantry through. Tank destroyers are poor in close combat against infantry and need their own all-round security and early warning of tanks. Both can help reduce bunkers.

## What a good bot does
- **Fire down the street, clear from the back, leave a way out** (tac.town)
  - Bypass with leading groups if possible; a following group clears.
  - Fire element suppresses street-facing windows; assault elements enter from the rear.
  - Assault sections alternate clearing and covering; fire element moves up in bounds.
  - Don't encircle: leave one retreat line and cover it with a fire element or tanks.
  - Defending: hold inside the built-up area, not on its edge.
- **Assault guns at the main effort, tank destroyers kept out of close combat** (tac.assault-gun)
  - Assault guns go with the infantry of the main effort, firing HE on the points that hold it up.
  - Tank destroyers wait in overwatch for tanks, away from close enemy infantry, with their own infantry or MG cover.
  - Either can fire on bunkers once enemy AT is suppressed.
- **One main effort, on the best-covered ground** (tac.main-effort)
  - Score axes by cover on the way in and by enemy strength; pick one.
  - Team: one bot or pair is main effort, the others hold or fix.
  - Bot: most maneuver groups on that axis; the rest press to split the enemy.
  - If a unit isn't stopped, it keeps going while neighbors are halted.

Figure: 4-layers/svg/f-town.svg

game.engine-binding:
# Engine binding

Maps each policy term to the input that tunes it. The engine-level adaptation of buying and tactical AI is a separate work and its own inputs are not known here. The nearest existing surface is the RobZ godny bot's `BotConfig` table (`resource/script/multiplayer/bot.data.lua`). Its keys and values are in `profiles/robz.yaml` under `bot_config`. This table is a read-only reference, not a design. Vanilla's bot data has only `MaxSquadSize`, `OrderRotationPeriod` and `FlagPriority`.

| Policy term | Nearest BotConfig keys (RobZ godny bot) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| main effort (axis, priority) | `Director`, `DirAttackRatio`, `DirDefendRatio`, `DirAvoid`, `FlagValueWeight`, `AttackSpread` | Director attacks at local ratio 1.4, defends at 1.1. Spread 0.8 rad gives three approaches. |

| fire and movement (bound) | `BoundStep`, `BoundEvery`, `BoundRatio`, `EngageDist`, `EngageHold`, `CoverRadius`, `UnderFireHold`, `UnderFireMaxMove` | 16 m bounds, 100 m engage distance. |
| assault line, capture | `LineGap`, `LineSpacing`, `LineMax`, `AssaultRatio`, `CaptureTeam`, `CapWalkDist` | Assault at local ratio 1.3. |
| dig in, fortify (defense layout) | `DigBands`, `DigSpacing`, `BuildSandbags`, `Fortify*`, `MGNests`, `Nest*` | Dig 15-35 m behind a held flag. |
| MG, sniper and AT-rifle siting | `MGMin/Want/Max`, `MGDigBack`, `MGLineBack`, `SniperMin/Want/Max`, `ATRMin/Want/Max` | Siting bands in units (20 = 1 m). |

| tank and TD standoff | `TankRange`, `TDRange`, `VehBack`, `VehMinInf`, `VehMinArmor`, `VehMinAT`, `FaceTolTank`, `FaceTolTD`, `VehStep` | Tanks fight armour at about 120 m, TDs at 170 m. |

| smoke | `Smoke`, `SmokeRange`, `SmokeCount`, `SmokeMaxFrac`, `SmokeEvery`, `SmokeAttackEvery` | 4 rounds at 45 m: front edge, both sides, middle. |
| grenades | `Grenades`, `GrenadeRange`, `AtGrenadeRange`, `GrenadeSafe` | 37 m, AT 22 m. |
| movement under threat | `DangerDist`, `Run`, `RunDist`, `CalmDist`, `PoseGap`, `ProneAfter` | Walk within 130 m of a known MG or vehicle. |
| force shape, role share, must-haves | `early`, `mid`, `late`, `antiTank`, `BotStrength`, `TDAfter`, `LightWhenArmour`, `AtNeedMax` | Composition tables by match stage. |
| money held back | `SaveForVehicles`, `SaveMinGroups`, `SaveMaxTime`, `BuyWaitBase`, `BuyWaitPerCost`, `BuyLead` | |
| withdrawal order | `Disengage` | Works in both mods. `no_retreat 1` (RobZ) only stops idle units retreating by auto-move; it never blocks an order. |

The bot author's replay numbers in the comments (for example "players fight armour at ~110 m") are not checked and are not doctrine.
game.ladder:
# Ladder: any game size

One rule: each bot plays the echelon its force supports, and the team plays one echelon above. All thresholds are starting values, `param_source: design`, unvalidated.

| Squads per bot | Bot plays as | Shape |
|---|---|---|
| up to about 6 | reinforced platoon | base of fire + 1 maneuver element |
| about 7 to 15 | company | support group, 2 maneuver groups, small reserve |
| about 16 to 28 | small battalion | company-size groups, support group, reserve |
| team of bots | one level up | one main effort across bots; the others hold or fix |

## How a decision moves down
| Level | Decides | Hands down |
|---|---|---|
| Team | where the main effort goes | axis and priority for each bot |
| Bot | how its force is split | a task for each group |
| Group | how to reach the task | bounds, positions, targets |
| Unit | reflexes | left to the engine and the mod |

Force grows during a match, so the shape is rechecked when squads on hand cross a threshold. A rise changes the shape at the next phase change, not mid-assault.
game.mechanics:
# Engine mechanics that shape doctrine (stock AS2 engine)

Read from the as64 notes (`run\docs\internal`:, limits AI/GPL/VIS/HUM) and the game files, 2026-11-08. Facts marked [T] in as64 are untested there and stay untested here. Mod values come from `profiles/*.yaml`.

## Unit stance logic (each soldier, once a second)
**Scope: AI auto-move only.** These values drive what a unit does on its own when it has no move order (idle, or holding a position). A move, attack or withdraw order from a player or from the bot command layer overrides them. So `no_retreat`, `advance_ratio` and `move_radius` change how units behave between orders, not what orders can make them do.
- threat = enemy strength near the unit; spread = own strength near it. retreatLimit = retreat_ratio x threat, advanceLimit = advance_ratio x spread, both x1.5 in cover.
- Advance: morale > 70 and threat > advanceLimit (charge if threat > 2x the limit).
- Retreat, unless `no_retreat`: spread > retreatLimit gives full retreat; morale < 50 falls back, < 30 retreats; a retreat holds until retreatLimit >= spread.
- Engine defaults: retreat 2, advance 2, move radius 7 m. **RobZ** sets no_retreat 1, advance 10, move radius 50: idle units never self-retreat, rarely self-advance, and roam up to 50 m on their own. A planned withdrawal is an order in both mods; RobZ only removes the unplanned one.

## Morale and fear
- Morale 0-100, regains about 0.83 per second. Damage costs damage x 20 and stops recovery for 10 s; morale is capped by health %.
- A death costs -60 morale shared among allies within 20 m; the killer gains +10. Allies pull 25% toward each other's morale.
- **No suppression model** (HUM-09): incoming fire that misses does nothing. "Pin" exists only as losses and fear.
- Frightened: health below 10% always, below 20% 70% of the time, below 30% 30% of the time.

## Cover and pose (AI soldiers)
- Seeks cover within 15 m (skips the flee 30% of the time); with no cover, flees 10-20 m.
- Approach pose: prone beyond 25 m of the target, crouched beyond 10 m, standing within 7 m.
- Self-heals below 70% health with a bandage after 5 s without seeing an enemy.

## Spotting
- Sight range = preset radius x scale x factor. Rule trees: the first matching branch wins and a deeper match **replaces** the factor, it does not multiply.
- A soldier who fired in the last second is seen farther (vanilla 1.15, RobZ 1.65 of radius), whatever his cover.
- Once a target is already seen (`visible`), its factor becomes 1.0 vanilla / 1.05 RobZ, so in RobZ a spotted standing man is tracked to ~87 m though first seen at ~124 m (as64 rule order, not checked in play).
- Still targets inside `uncover` range are spotted whatever their pose.
- Recognition: a contact counts once time seen > distance / sight x RecognizeTime. Engine default 2 s, vanilla 0.25 s, RobZ 0.01 s: near instant in both mods.
- Contacts are shared over InformRange (vanilla 40 m, RobZ 120 m). Unseen contacts are remembered 120 s.
- Haze and weather do not cut AI sight. Night factor 0.13, but most vanilla map presets switch the penalty off; lit targets are fully seen.
- **Concealment correction (2026-11-08):** RobZ does not make concealment worth less. Contact comes earlier, but cover and prone cut sight more (3.75x against 2.5x in vanilla).

## Smoke
- Wind does not move bullets, grenades or smoke (VIS-16). The "wind" part of smoke doctrine is out in game.
- Vanilla smoke grenade: screen builds over 5 s, lasts about 60 s. Mortar smoke builds in 2-5 s, about 60 s in both mods.
- RobZ grenade, launcher and shell smoke: about 90 s, plus a sight-blocking sphere (106.8 units, about 5 m) for 87 s; white phosphorus 40-60 s; large smoke 120 s.
- Throw range: vanilla 25 m, RobZ 32 m.

## Targeting and vehicles
- A contact no target group matches is never attacked (AI-01).
- A vehicle has one target list for all its weapons (AI-06): its MGs wait while the gun hunts a tank. AI vehicle MGs fire about one burst per 1.3 s.
- Hatch gunners leave their MG when threat is above 4x. Bailed crews may re-enter after 20 s; stock bots do not re-crew (AI-13).
- A vehicle that cannot aim detours every 2-4 s, which makes it circle. Aim delay 0.3-1.1 s.
- HE blast falls linearly to zero at its radius; penetration ends at range + 5 m. Towed guns cannot fire.

## What stock bots can and cannot order
- Bot Lua can only Spawn, CaptureFlag and SayChat (AI-12, MIS-08). No artillery fire missions (AI-11). Grenade ammo drops and flamethrowers need direct control (GPL-16).
- Vanilla `bot.data.lua`: squads of 5, orders rotate every 3 min, flag priority captured 1 / enemy 2 / neutral 3.
- Unit limits give no refund on death.

## What this changes in the doctrine mapping
| Doctrine idea | In game |
|---|---|
| Suppress, then assault | Proxy: losses and fear only. Kill or blind (smoke) the base of fire instead of pinning it. |
| Concealment, hold fire | Direct, and stronger in RobZ: prone in cover is seen at 33 m against 124 m standing in the open. Firing reveals at once (1.65 factor). |
| Ambush | Direct if the ambusher is still, outside the enemy's uncover range, and holds fire until the set range. |
| Smoke and wind | Smoke blinds as doctrine says; wind is out; life is fixed per mod. |
| Withdrawal | Always an order in both mods. Auto-move only: vanilla idle units also fall back alone when outnumbered by the retreat ratio; RobZ idle units never do (no_retreat). |
| Short bounds | RobZ starts stamina at 50 with slow regain: walk inside danger range, sprint only short dashes. |

# Roles

Doctrine rules name roles, never unit names, so they work on any mod. A role is read from unit data; anything that can't be classified goes on the mod's review list and is treated as `rifle` or `vehicle_other` until mapped.

| Role | Doctrine branch | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| rifle | infantry | maneuver, holding ground |
| smg | infantry | assault, close terrain |
| mg | mg | base of fire |
| mortar | mortar | indirect support, smoke where the mod has it |
| at_infantry | at | close anti-tank |
| at_gun | at | anti-tank screen, depth |
| tank | tank | shock, support of the assault |
| assault_gun | tank | direct fire support of infantry |
| td | at | anti-tank overwatch |
| recon | recon | finding the enemy, screening |
| engineer | engineer | obstacles, mines |
| artillery | artillery | fire support; stock bots can't call it (AI-11) |
| sniper | infantry | picking targets, recon |

The mapping method is reused from `ai spawn improved for robz 1.30.x\tools\build_unit_meta.py`. Godny's role list in `bot.units.lua` is reference only.
game.translation:
# Translation: doctrine terms to game terms

Doctrine says what good play is. This file restates it in terms that hold on any mod and any game size. It does not say how the engine does it; that link is `engine-binding.md`. Engine behaviour behind the numbers is in `mechanics.md`; profile fields are explained in `profiles/fields.md`.

| Doctrine term | Game term | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Echelon | Force group | Set by squads on hand, from `ladder.md`. Never by map name. |
| Branch | Role | Read from unit data, per `roles.md`. |
| Phase | Match phase | Set by flags, force ratio and tempo. See below. |
| Terrain | Feature class | open, woods, town, ridge, river, road. |
| Distance | Ratio of a profile value | `0.6 x mg` means 60% of the profile's median MG range. Doctrine yards are never used directly. |
| Time | Distance over unit speed | Doctrinal minutes do not fit match length. |
| Nation | Army family | From the profile's `armies` table. Unknown armies use the universal core. |

## Match phases
A **phase change** is the moment a group's or team's phase moves from one row of this table to another. It's the only safe time to change force shape or reassign groups.

| Phase | Enters when | Leaves when |
|---|---|---|
| approach | no contact on the chosen axis | first contact |
| recon | contact, enemy line unclear | enemy positions on the axis are known, or the time allowance ends |
| attack | local force ratio favors us at the chosen point | objective reached, or the attack stalls |
| assault | assault group inside close range of the objective | objective held or lost |
| defense | local force ratio is against us, or we hold what we want | ratio turns in our favor |
| counterattack | a held point was just lost and a reserve exists | point retaken or reserve spent |
| withdrawal | group cannot hold and has somewhere to go | group is rejoined with the next position |

Starting values for "favors" and "stalled" are design values, not doctrine, and are untested.

## Distances
Every distance in a rule names its base: `mg`, `rifle`, `gun_medium`, `sight_open` (standing man in the open), `sight_cover_prone` (prone man in cover) or `uncover` (still target auto-spotted). The profile supplies the number, so one rule stays valid across mods. A doctrinal yardage goes in the claim as evidence; the ratio in the rule is marked `param_source: design` or `tuned`, unless the source itself states the proportion. A value read from the mod profile (such as smoke life) is `param_source: profile`.

## Fit tags
- `direct`: the game has it.
- `proxy`: must be approximated.
- `engine`: depends on the adaptation.
- `out`: not in the game, such as supply or long preparatory fires.

Known stock limits to recheck against the adaptation (details in `mechanics.md`): no suppression model, so "pin then assault" is a proxy; morale is capped by health. Stock bots have no artillery fire missions (AI-11). Bailed crews are not re-crewed (AI-13). Stock bot Lua can order only `Spawn`, `CaptureFlag` and `SayChat` (MIS-08). Wind moves nothing, so smoke wind rules are out. In RobZ, idle units on AI auto-move never self-retreat; ordered moves are unaffected.
game.worked-examples:
# Worked examples, on paper

Nothing here has been played. Each example applies the cards to a profile, to test that the translation holds together. Metres below are worked from the profile medians and move with the mod, so they aren't parameters.

| Term | Formula | Vanilla | RobZ | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Attack width W, company shape | 1.0 x mg | 100 | 150 | base design |
| Defense width | 2 x W | 200 | 300 | ratio claim |
| Delay width | 4 x W | 400 | 600 | ratio claim |
| Base of fire stands | 0.6 to 0.8 x mg | 60-80 | 90-120 | design |
| AT guns hold fire to | 0.6 x gun_medium | 72 | 114 | design |
| Assault starts | 0.5 x rifle | 35 | 38 | design |
| Lines at most | 1.0 x mg | 100 | 150 | claim, Soviet |
| Vision radius, raw | profile `vision_m` | 70 | 110 | game data |
| Human vision against humans | radius x scale x rule | 52 | 124 | derived from game data |

## 1v1, vanilla, 5 squads, attack a village
1. **Shape** (force.shape-by-size): reinforced platoon, one base of fire and one maneuver element.
2. **Buy** (force.combined-arms-minimum): MG first, rifles, light AT.
3. **Axis** (tac.main-effort): the best-covered way in, scored on the map. With one bot there is one axis.
4. **Width** (tac.frontage): half of W, about 50, since it's a platoon rather than a company (design).
5. **Attack** (tac.fire-and-move, tac.assault-timing): the MG sets up obliquely at 60 to 80, rifles go by cover, assault from about 35, and the MG shifts to the flank when masked.
6. **After** (tac.consolidate): past the objective, MG forward, into cover.

**Problem found:** vanilla's base of fire stands beyond human vision (52 m). The group needs a spotter forward, or the base must come closer. Listed in test notes.

## 4v4, RobZ, 12 squads per bot, attack along a ridge
1. **Shape:** each bot plays a company. The team plays one level up.
2. **Team** (tac.main-effort): one pair of bots is the main effort on the best-covered axis. The other pair fixes along the ridge: each holds its flags, keeps fire on the enemy facing it, and pushes only far enough to stop that enemy shifting to the main axis. It doesn't try to break through.
3. **Each bot:** support group, two maneuver groups, a small support held back. Width about 150 each.
4. **Fire:** base at 90 to 120. Human vision of 124 lets it see for itself, unlike vanilla.
5. **Armor seen** (force.counter-buy, tac.at-screen): mass AT if strength is unknown. Guns hold to about 114, but RobZ recognition (0.01 s) makes surprise weak, so test that ratio.
6. **Stall** (tac.reserve): commit the support whole at a flank, then rebuild it.
7. **Falling back** (tac.withdrawal): `no_retreat 1` only affects auto-move: idle soldiers won't leave alone. The bot's withdraw order works as usual, and it has to come before the group is pinned.

## 8v8, unknown mod, 6 squads per bot, defend
1. **Profile first:** extract ranges and vision. Unmapped armies use the universal core and roles come from unit data. Until extracted, every distance below stays as a ratio.
2. **Shape:** platoon per bot. Eight bots form a team-level plan.
3. **Team:** forward bots on the approaches and two bots back as the reserve (tac.defense-layout, tac.reserve). Eight narrow fronts leave gaps, so cover the gaps with fire instead of thinning groups (tac.frontage).
4. **Each bot:** two parts forward, one back. Depth 0.5 to 1.0 x rifle. Rifles hold to effective range.
5. **Lost point** (tac.counterattack): the nearest back group goes at once into the flank, fire across the base, stop at the old line.

**Problem found:** nearly all bots at platoon shape means team-level reserve matters more than bot-level reserve. The ladder says so, but the threshold where this flips is untested.

## What the examples show
- The formulas produce usable numbers on both profiles with no doctrine yards.
- Vanilla's vision is shorter than the base-of-fire standoff, the first conflict between a doctrine ratio and game data.
- RobZ's `rifle` p10 of 4 m is a misclassified weapon in the extraction, so use medians. Worth cleaning in the profile build.

# Personas (larp)

Load only when a lobby names a persona or nation style. fidelity 0 plays the core rules; 1 copies the period, flaws included. Traits marked lore are design, not sourced, and apply only at fidelity 0.7 or more; departs = breaks doctrine on purpose. Retreat settings steer only idle units on AI auto-move.

## universal (core, fidelity 0)
armies: axis_minor; voice neutral; temperament aggression 0.5, reserve_share 0.2, initiative 0.6, caution 0.5
note: Fallback for unknown armies; plays the core rules only.

## us-1944-rifle (us, fidelity 0.6)
armies: usa; voice us; temperament aggression 0.5, reserve_share 0.25, initiative 0.6, caution 0.6
- tac.fire-and-move: Lead with fire: mortars and MGs on the objective before any rifle squad moves. [company.infantry.attack company.mortar.attack]
- tac.reverse-slope: Put the main line on the reverse slope when the forward slope is under observed fire. [c-US-3001]
- tac.infiltration: Counter infiltration with posts that hold alone and a reserve that strikes hard. [company.infantry.infiltration]
note: Methodical; strong with support weapons, slow without them.

## uk-1944-infantry (uk, fidelity 0.6)
armies: eng; voice uk; temperament aggression 0.4, reserve_share 0.25, initiative 0.5, caution 0.7
- tac.smoke: Screen every crossing of open ground; move once the smoke is thick. [company.infantry.smoke]
- tac.consolidate: Consolidate at once on each objective before the next bound. [squad.infantry.assault]
note: Careful and smoke-heavy; rarely overextends.

## ger-1944-kampfgruppe (ger, fidelity 0.7)
armies: ger, ger2, ger_ss; voice ger; temperament aggression 0.7, reserve_share 0.3, initiative 0.8, caution 0.4
- tac.counterattack: Counterattack a lost position at once, close behind the fire, at the flank of the break-in. [c-GER-0044]
- tac.mg-defense: Build strongpoints round MGs, heavy mortars and an SP gun, firing all round. [c-GER-3021]
- tac.main-effort: One narrow main effort with the heavy weapons massed behind it. [battalion.infantry.attack]
note: Aggressive counterattacks; dangerous to push into. German doctrine here is reported by other nations.

## su-1941-rifle (su, fidelity 0.9)
armies: rus; voice su; temperament aggression 0.9, reserve_share 0.1, initiative 0.2, caution 0.1
- tac.main-effort: Attack straight down the ordered axis; do not shift to a found gap. [lore] [departs]
- tac.withdrawal: Hold or counterattack; withdraw only on a direct order from the top. [lore] [departs]
- tac.reserve: Feed the reserve into a stalled attack rather than holding it back. [lore] [departs]
note: Larp lore, not doctrine: frontal and costly on purpose. Its own manuals asked for initiative; this persona plays the 1941 reputation.

## su-1944-guards (su, fidelity 0.7)
armies: rus_guard, rus; voice su; temperament aggression 0.8, reserve_share 0.2, initiative 0.7, caution 0.4
- tac.main-effort: Mass most forces and fire on the main blow where ground gives cover and observation. [c-SU-2001]
- tac.pursuit: On finding a gap, leaders push through on their own, even off direction. [c-SU-0018]
- tac.town: Fix a town frontally with part; send the main blow round to its rear. [c-SU-3019]
note: Heavy, fast main blow and bold exploitation.

## jp-1942-infantry (jp, fidelity 0.8)
armies: jap; voice jp; temperament aggression 0.9, reserve_share 0.15, initiative 0.7, caution 0.2
- tac.bait: Fake strength in front with noise and automatic fire while the main force goes round a flank. [c-JP-2003]
- tac.infiltration: Under a holding attack, send LMG and grenade patrols round the flanks into the rear. [c-JP-2005]
- tac.night: Prefer attacks when vision is short. [company.infantry.night]
- tac.withdrawal: When a group is losing, charge instead of falling back. [lore] [departs]
note: Flanking and night attacks; at high fidelity it charges when losing. All doctrine here is reported by the US and UK.

## fi-1940-winter (fi, fidelity 0.8)
armies: none; voice fi; temperament aggression 0.6, reserve_share 0.2, initiative 0.9, caution 0.6
- tac.counter-sniper: Use snipers heavily from hides, as reported of Finnish practice. [c-FI-3001 c-FI-3002]
- tac.ambush: Ambush road-bound columns from the woods. [company.infantry.ambush battalion.infantry.winter]
- tac.pursuit: Cut a stalled column into pockets and destroy them one by one. [lore]
note: Needs a mod with a Finnish army or a winter map; maps to no stock army. Finnish practice here is reported.

## what-if-modern (core, fidelity 0)
armies: none; voice neutral; temperament aggression 0.6, reserve_share 0.25, initiative 0.9, caution 0.5
- modern: m.ooda, m.mission-command, m.recon-pull, m.find-fix-finish, m.culmination
note: Not period play: re-plans on events, commits the reserve behind success. For comparison against period personas.
core:
# Core

Roles: rifle, smg, mg, mortar, at_infantry, at_gun, tank, assault_gun, td, recon, engineer, artillery, sniper. Read from unit data. Unmapped infantry counts as rifle; an unmapped vehicle is `vehicle_other`, used for transport, not for a fighting role. A tank can serve as base or maneuver.

Shape, by squads per bot (`design`, untested):
- up to 6: reinforced platoon. Base of fire + 1 maneuver element.
- 7 to 15: company. Support group, 2 maneuver groups, small reserve.
- 16 to 28: small battalion. Company-size groups, support group, reserve.
- Team: one level up. One main effort; the other bots hold or fix.

Recheck shape when squads cross a threshold. Change it at the next phase change, not during an assault.

Words: `support group` is the base of fire. `Reserve` is what is held back, which US manuals call the support. `Company-shape` means a bot of 7 to 15 squads. `Local ratio` is our strength against his within 1.0 x mg of the point (`design`). `Pin` means hurt, under stock limits below.

Decisions: team picks main effort, bot splits force, group picks route and targets, unit reflexes stay with the engine or mod.

Phases:
- approach: no contact on the axis.
- recon: contact, enemy line unclear.
- attack: local ratio favors us at the chosen point.
- assault: assault group in close range of the objective.
- defense: ratio against us, or we hold what we want.
- counterattack: a held point just fell and a reserve exists.
- withdrawal: group can't hold and has somewhere to go.

Distance: always a ratio of a profile base, such as `0.6 x mg`. Never doctrinal yards. A distance beyond `vision_m` needs a spotter, or use the vision distance (`design`). Time: distance over unit speed, from unit data. Army: the profile maps it to a doctrine family; unknown armies use no flavor.

Fit: `direct` the game has it, `proxy` approximate, `engine` depends on the adaptation, `out` skip.

Stock limits, recheck against the adaptation (codes are entries in the as64 limits list): no suppression model and morale follows health, so "pin then assault" is a proxy. No bot artillery fire missions (AI-11). Bailed crews aren't re-crewed (AI-13). One target list per vehicle (AI-06). Stock bot Lua orders only Spawn, CaptureFlag, SayChat (MIS-08).
readme:
# Men of War doctrine pack

WW2 small-unit tactics, read from period manuals and restated for the Assault Squad 2 bot AI on vanilla, RobZ or any mod.

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `atlas.html` | The whole pack as one page. Open it in a browser; it needs no network. |
| `markdown/` | The same doctrine as small text files for an AI to load a piece at a time. Start at `markdown/INDEX.md`. |
| `sdk/doctrine.json`, `sdk/doctrine.lua` | Schema 1: 38 rules, 9 personas, 7 voices, 10 missions, 2 mod profiles. |
| `sdk/SCHEMA.md`, `sdk/README.md` | Data format and the tools that make and check it. |
| `sdk/missions/` | One briefing per mission kit. |
| `sdk/samples/`, `sdk/aar/` | Sample match logs, the reports made from them, and a blank answer sheet for the scenario test set. |

## Markdown layer, from short to deep

1. `INDEX.md` routes a task to the files it needs.
2. `core.md`, `profiles/<mod>.md`, `cards/<rule>.md`: what to do. A typical task loads under 10 KB.
3. `cells/<compartment>.md`: the method behind a card, every line cited, plus known gaps.
4. `evidence/<compartment>.md`: the cited claims, with document, leaf and page.
5. `game/`: how doctrine maps to the game. `sdk/`: missions, voices, tests, reports, schema.
6. `personas.md` and `modern.md`: only when a lobby names a persona or asks for post-war ideas.

## Limits

- Nothing here has been played in a match. Values marked `design` are starting guesses.
- Germany is mostly described by other armies; Japan and Italy only by others.
- Claims are restated in my own words with citations. No scans or long quotes are included.
- The SDK tools themselves run from the source folder, which holds the claim files they read.
